newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer indicator falls, first time in 14 mths.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer indicator falls, first time in 14 mths.

text.p: The NTC consumer industries' leading indicator fell in December for the first time in 14 months, having reached record highs in each of the previous six months.

"The sharp rise in the indicator last year signals a considerable increase in economic activity in 1997, but the latest dip is the first indication of a downturn in the rate of economic growth for 14 months, suggesting the possibility of a turning point in late 1997," NTC, a specialist provider of business research and information, said.
NTC's indicator is compiled from a wide range of economic variables which it says give advance indications of turning points in economic activity, usually leading the cycle by 11 months.
The decline in the indicator in December was due to falls in four of the eight component series:

Output of consumer goods, as measured by the Purchasing Managers' Survey, showed weaker growth; December TV advertising revenues were subdued relative to recent months; economic optimism, as measured by MORI, fell sharply and the rate of growth of retail sales fell back.
